description: We are a multidisciplinary engineering, simulation, and spatial-data team building physics-grounded navigation tools for human planetary exploration. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we created ARES-WALK to turn orbital and rover datasets from Gale Crater into a real-time Mars EVA survival workstation.
summary: ARES-WALK is a hyperlocalized Mars Extravehicular Activity (EVA) planning and field-execution workstation built for the Altadena boxwork unit on Lower Mount Sharp, Gale Crater (4.80°S, 137.38°E; NASA Curiosity Sols 4535–4611). Addressing the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, it bridges orbital terrain mapping with surface crew safety by combining six raster modalities (elevation, slope, boxwork TPI ridges, thermal inertia, CRISM D2300 clay index, and sand fraction) with a 0.38g spacesuit metabolic model, an interactive 360° terrain-twin visor, and stitched NASA Mastcam panoramas. By enforcing a mandatory 25% PLSS walkback reserve at every waypoint and computing minimum-dose shelter routes during Solar Particle Events, ARES-WALK helps astronauts explore rugged Martian terrain safely.
details:
Live Workstation: https://gittanish.github.io/ares-walk/

Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/GitTanish/ares-walk

What It Does & How It Works:

ARES-WALK is a hyperlocalized Extravehicular Activity (EVA) planning and field-execution workstation built for the Altadena boxwork unit on Lower Mount Sharp, Gale Crater (4.80°S, 137.38°E; NASA Curiosity Sols 4535–4611). It connects orbital mission planning with surface navigation through a two-stage pipeline:

1. Python Ingestion & Panorama Stitching (`src/pds_ingest.py`, `src/build_mastcam_panos.py`, `src/mars_eva_engine.py`): Aligns 27 real JPL MMGIS Curiosity traverse waypoints and 10 science stations (ALT-01 to ALT-10) onto a local East-North-Up (ENU) metric grid, fetches verified MAST_LEFT frames from the NASA Mars Raw Images API, stitches wide-field cylindrical mosaics for landmark outcrops (ALT-05 Layered Spur and ALT-10 Upper Bench) using rover azimuth/elevation pointing telemetry, and precomputes a 45-step baseline EVA timeline.

2. Dual-Mode Browser Workstation (`index.html`):

- Tactical 2D GIS Console: Renders 6 terrain and spectral layers (HiRISE Elevation, Slope, Boxwork TPI Ridges, THEMIS Thermal Inertia, CRISM D2300 Clay Index, and Aeolian Sand Fraction) alongside ray-traced UHF relay viewsheds and an interactive elevation/PLSS walkback profile. Clicking anywhere on the map runs an 8-connected Dijkstra solver to evaluate out-and-back metabolic cost for custom side-trip waypoints.

- 360° Field Visor: Combines an interactive 360° terrain-twin panorama (with conformal route projection and a synchronized PiP mini-map) with a real NASA Mastcam frame and drag-to-pan mosaic viewer.

- Emergency SPE Radiation Abort: Clicking "Simulate SPE Flare" (85 mSv/h) aborts unvisited stations and solves a minimum-time shelter sprint route back to the pressurized rover under the 50 mSv acute dose limit.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Regional Mars maps do not tell an astronaut whether a detour across loose aeolian sand will leave enough suit consumables to get back to shelter. ARES-WALK turns planetary datasets into an operational survival tool that protects EVA crews against metabolic exhaustion, communication dead zones, steep terrain hazards, and sudden solar radiation storms.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

- Strict 25% Walkback Reserve Rule: Enforces a mandatory 100 Wh (25%) PLSS floor at every traverse node using asymmetric terrain-aware return routing rather than straight-line distance.

- Gravity-Scaled Biomechanics: Adapts the Pandolf metabolic equation to Mars gravity (3.72 m/s², 0.38g), accounting for 78 kg crew mass + 52 kg PLSS load, slope grade, and sand slip penalties, plus O₂ and sublimator cooling water budgets.

- Transparent Data Provenance: Every raster layer displays a dynamic badge distinguishing genuine loaded PDS products from the calibrated digital twin fallback.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Languages: Python 3, HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript

- Libraries & APIs: NumPy, OpenCV, Pillow, HTML5 2D Canvas API, NASA/JPL MSL Raw Images API, JPL MMGIS Waypoints JSON

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub & GitHub Pages
